chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hammad ibn Abi Talha, from Mu'adh ibn Kathir, who said:

I looked at the standing place (Arafat) and the people in it were many, so I approached Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'The people at the standing place are very numerous.' He turned his gaze and swept it over them, then said, 'Come closer to me, O Abu Abdillah. They are scum which the waves have brought from every place. No, by Allah, the Hajj is not except for you. No, by Allah, Allah will not accept (the Hajj) except from you.'

key_terms.الْمَوْقِف: The standing place, specifically Arafat during Hajj
key_terms.غُثَاء: Scum or froth, used metaphorically for the masses
key_terms.يَتَقَبَّلُ: He accepts (referring to divine acceptance of deeds)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn say about the validity of Hajj for the general crowd versus the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Mu'adh ibn Kathir observes the vast multitude at Arafat and asks Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (as) about them. The Imam characterizes the general crowd as 'ghutha' (scum/foam) carried by waves, using the metaphor to distinguish the superficial mass from the core of true devotion. He asserts that the Hajj is exclusively for the Ahl al-Bayt and that Allah accepts only from them, highlighting the Shia concept of *khassah* (the elite) in spiritual acceptance.
